body: The eventTypeId fragment is `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` with no outer parentheses. When it is the only filter, `buildFilterConditions` returns it unwrapped, and `getFilterConditions()` is public. A caller that writes `WHERE ${filterConditions} AND ${somethingElse}` (or ANDs it with auth conditions itself) gets `a OR (b AND ...)` because AND binds tighter than OR. The date range or authorization clause would then be skipped for rows matching `eventTypeId`, which leaks data. `getBaseConditions` only avoids this because it happens to wrap each side. Wrap the fragment itself: `(("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X))`. The OR-joined results from `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`/`buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` should also be parenthesized so every returned fragment can be composed safely.

`InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` makes `teamId` optional for every scope, so the compiler no longer catches `{ scope: "team" }` without a `teamId`. That call now type-checks, the zod `safeParse` fails at runtime, `options` becomes null, and the service quietly returns `1=0` (no data) instead of raising a compile error. Keep the constructor typed with the discriminated union (`InsightsBookingServiceOptions`), or at least log/throw when validation fails.

This PR removes `findMany` and adds `getBaseConditions`, which changes the public contract: callers now have to build raw SQL and interpolate these fragments. The fragments use bare column names (`"userId"`, `"teamId"`, ...) with no table qualifier. If a caller joins `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` to `Booking`, `Team`, `users` or similar tables, these references become ambiguous (a Postgres error) or bind to the wrong table. Either qualify the columns (for example `"BookingTimeStatusDenormalized"."userId"` or a documented alias) or document that the fragment is only valid against an unjoined `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized`.

`getAuthorizationConditions()` always returns a non-null `Prisma.Sql` (it falls back to `1=0`), so the `else if (filterConditions)` branch and the final `NOTHING_CONDITION` branch can never run. If auth ever became nullable, this code would apply the filter conditions with no authorization. Simplify to `filterConditions ? sql`(${auth}) AND (${filter})` : auth` so auth is always applied.

The whole "Caching" describe block was deleted rather than updated to the new SQL format. The service still caches `cachedAuthConditions` and `cachedFilterConditions`, and that behavior now has no test. The only real query test runs against the DB with a filter; nothing exercises a filter-less or eventTypeId-only query. That combination is where the operator-precedence problem shows up. Restore the caching tests and add `$queryRaw` coverage for the team, org and eventTypeId-only paths. The generated SQL is now only checked by string equality, which cannot catch a query that is syntactically valid but semantically wrong.
